references.text: God's command to eat unleavened bread for seven days during the Feast of Unleavened Bread, explaining why the Israelites baked unleavened cakes.
The Egyptians urged the people to leave the land in haste, and the Israelites took their dough with them before it was leavened.
The Lord foretold that Pharaoh would drive the Israelites out of Egypt by force.
The Lord said that Pharaoh would drive them completely out of Egypt after the final plague.
Reminder to eat unleavened bread because they left Egypt in haste, called 'the bread of affliction'.
Lot baked unleavened cakes for the angels, an early example of unleavened bread in connection with haste.
The verses belong to the same event; 12:20 gives the command that 12:39 shows was fulfilled in haste.
The law concerning the feast (Exodus 23) anchors its meaning directly in the event from chapter 12.
